name: Get the Scoop
summary: Near the Mirage Raceway, Magus Tirth has forgotten the words to open his sealed strongbox. His apprentice, Johnson, is missing somewhere around the track, and Tirth needs the spellbook inside.

sections.title: A Magus and His Memory
sections.body: Magus Tirth lives on the cracked salt bed of the Shimmering Flats in Thousand Needles. He is an eccentric spellcaster whose arcane knowledge and books draw mages seeking to advance. Patience helps when dealing with him. Tirth relies on an assistant for everyday details, even the spoken passwords guarding his arcane stores. Now a book of power is locked away, and the magic words have slipped from his mind entirely.

sections.title: Fowl Play
sections.body: Goblins and gnomes who run the Mirage Raceway can tell you what happened to Johnson, Magus Tirth's apprentice. Tirth turned Johnson into a common chicken, and the apprentice now wanders the salt flats unable to speak. When you draw near, the spell's haze lifts for a moment. Johnson can squawk out the missing password.

faq.answer: Magus Tirth is a reclusive human wizard near the Mirage Raceway in the Shimmering Flats of Thousand Needles. Mages seek his advanced arcane lore to hone their craft.

faq.q: Why does Tirth need the password to his own box?
faq.answer: Tirth locked his strongbox with a spoken phrase and relied on his assistant to remember such everyday details. When his apprentice vanished, Tirth forgot the words.
Johnson wanders near the racetrack east of Tirth's camp. Finding him is harder because Tirth turned him into a chicken.

faq.q: Why was the apprentice turned into a chicken?
faq.answer: Tirth cursed Johnson, then forgot he had done so. When he learned what had become of his assistant, he vaguely assumed Johnson deserved it for being an ungrateful pupil.

aliases: what book is in the chest
faq.answer: Tirth's strongbox holds a book of rituals, instructions essential to a mage's continuing education, and magical implements.

aliases: can non mages do get the scoop
faq.answer: Only mages seeking specialized instruction and materials to craft a potent wand can undertake this trial.

angles.text: As a mage, dealing with Tirth shows the perils of polymorph curses and the absent-mindedness that can afflict powerful scholars.
